text:
mike: quick sync — thinking about changing autoscaler to use an amortized credit curve instead of discrete burst tokens. aim: smoother ramp for tenants that have spiky but short-lived traffic.
anya: sounds interesting. can you sketch failure modes? esp on noisy tenants that oscillate.
mike: main risk is slow drain of credits causing sustained over-provisioning if a tenant has repeated short spikes. mitigation: decay curve + hard cap and a per-tenant debt ceiling.
jess: curious how this interacts with prewarm. we currently prewarm on token threshold, which is binary. blending with a continuous credit makes admission logic more complex.
mike: agreed — proposal: keep prewarm trigger but scale prewarm size proportional to amortized credit level. small config change.
sam: can we see a sample config? makes it easier to judge operator ergonomics.
mike: sure — rough idea:
```yaml
pool_autoscaler:
  credit_model: amortized
  amortization_window_s: 120
  credit_decay_half_life_s: 30
  per_tenant_credit_cap: 200
  prewarm:
    trigger_threshold: 0.7 # fraction of cap
    size_multiplier: 0.25 # of tenant baseline capacity
```
anya: nice. a few thoughts: 1) metrics — need amortized_credit gauge in tenant metrics pipeline. 2) billing/visibility — customers will ask why they have "hidden credits". 3) safety — add eviction preconditions when cluster pressure high.
jess: +1 on metrics and billing. can we expose a debug endpoint showing credit burn / decay for a tenant window? ephemeral read-only.
mike: yes — operator API: `/debug/tenants/{id}/credits?window=2m` returning a small timeseries. orch-bot: deploy-check: found a lint warning in autoscaler proto (missing decimal field docs).
mike: thanks orch-bot. on the safety side: proposal adds two hard constraints: a) global headroom floor (reserve N GPUs for GC) b) emergency reclaim that sets all amortized credits to zero when offered capacity < 5% for >1m.
sam: how about fairness? if a noisy tenant burns credits and then sits idle, should credits slowly return or should there be a reclamation priority for smaller tenants? jess: i'd prefer symmetric decay and an admin knob to zero a tenant. manual reclaim via console is fine for now.
mike: implementation plan: 1) proto + config change (low risk) 2) metrics + debug endpoint 3) small autoscaler sim with historical traces to validate economics 4) deploy to staging with canary for 48h.
anya: can you drop links to the sim and proto in this thread? i'll join the staging run.
mike: will do — pushing a draft proto PR tonight, and a sim notebook (colab) tomorrow. action: mike -> proto PR, jess -> debug endpoint, anya/sam -> staging canary. :thumbsup:
jess: :thumbsup:
anya: i'll add on-call playbook blurb for emergency reclaim.
mike: cool — follow-up sync Friday 10am. thanks everyone.
